name: Atomic updates
problem: Concurrent read-modify-write of one counter can lose increments even when reads and writes individually complete.

origin.summary: Historical priority, inventor and first adoption remain unresolved. The cited primary documentation establishes the described mechanism, not its invention.

mechanism: An atomic read-modify-write combines observation and update as one operation. Memory ordering controls synchronization with other accesses; atomicity of one location is not a transaction over arbitrary state.
transferRule: Separate indivisibility of a location from ordering of surrounding operations.
confidence: MEDIUM: mechanism anchored to primary documentation; historical attribution and unknown language cells unresolved; traces are editorial reasoning examples.
examples: Two fetch_add(1) operations on an AtomicUsize initially0 return distinct old values0 and1; after joining both workers, the counter is2.
counterexamples: Two separately atomic counters can temporarily violate their combined invariant.

assessment.prompt: A flag announces that a buffer is ready. Why is an atomic flag alone insufficient without an ordering protocol?
rubric: Distinguish atomic flag storage from publication of buffer writes.
